newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia PM changes party lineup.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia PM changes party lineup.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad has made changes at the top of his party without touching the government, but political analysts said on Friday they believed a cabinet reshuffle was in the works.

Mahathir, president of the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), said the changes to the party's Supreme Council, its highest decision-making body, late on Thursday would have no effect on his cabinet.

"We don't have a cabinet reshuffle," Mahathir was quoted as saying by the Bernama news agency after he dropped Youth and Sports Minister Muhyiddin Yassin and Rural Development Minister Annuar Musa from the UMNO Supreme Council.

Information Minister Mohamed Rahmat, who was the party's secretary-general for eight years, was demoted to ordinary council member. UMNO information chief Hussein Ahmad was also made a council member.

"I think there will be a Cabinet reshuffle but Mahathir doesn't want to do it immediately as he does not want to be seen reacting to speculation by the press," Jomo Kwame Sundaram, an economics professor with the Universiti Malaya in Kuala Lumpur, told Reuters.
"He (Mahathir) will want to allow a decent interval until the press stops talking about. It could be next month or even next year," said Sundaram.
Positions in UMNO are viewed as having great significance because they usually dictate who's who in government.

The party is the largest in the National Front coalition, which has ruled Malaysia since independence from Britain in 1957. UMNO's president and deputy have traditionally been prime minister and deputy prime minister.
The party's elections every three years are regarded as more important than the national polls held every five years.

Under the party constitution, the president is empowered to appoint members to the Supreme Council if they can't win a seat in the UMNO elections. The Supreme Council has 45 members, including 10 appointed members.
Mahathir named eight of the appointed members on Thursday, leaving the party to guess who would fill the other two seats.

International Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz, Defence Minister Syed Hamid Albar, Perak state Chief Minister Ramli Ngah Talib and Negri Sembilan state Chief Minister Isa Samad -- all losers in the last UMNO elections in October -- were among the eight Mahathir appointed.
An UMNO official said speculation was rife that the vacant seats were for Tengku Razaleigh Hamzah and Rais Yatim, two former rivals of Mahathir who had returned to the UMNO fold.
"If Razaleigh and Rais are appointed to the Supreme Council, they could eventually be returning to the government," said the UMNO official, who declined to be identified.
Razaleigh, a former trade minister in Mahathir's Cabinet, recently disbanded his opposition Spirit of 46 party to rejoin UMNO with Rais, the deputy president of Spirit and a former foreign minister.
